name: assistantlabs
description: Customer conversations, CRM, leads, bookings, help desk and social posts for small and medium businesses that use AssistantLabs.

interface.longDescription:
AssistantLabs connects ChatGPT to your AssistantLabs workspace, where small and medium businesses manage customer conversations, leads, bookings, tasks and social posts, and where an AI agent answers customers on their messaging channels.

What you can do:
• Setup: follow the same four setup steps as the AssistantLabs app, build your AI agent from your website, pick your channels and tools, and get one link that connects them
• Conversations: see who is waiting for a reply, search what customers said, label a conversation, and reply to a customer
• Contacts: look up customers and companies, add a contact, and update a contact's details
• Leads: see the leads board, add and move leads, and log what happened with each one
• Bookings: check free slots, list appointments, and book, confirm, cancel or complete them
• Social posts: write, edit and publish posts, and see how they performed
• AI agent: add instructions, change its tone, and update its FAQ, links, catalog, guidelines and business details
• Help desk: read, assign, note and resolve tickets
• Tasks: view, create and update tasks
• Reports: see your money summary, open invoices and payments, marketing overview, ads and campaign results, and landing pages
• Ads: pause a running ad

Who it is for: owners and staff of small and medium businesses that already use AssistantLabs.

Limitations:
• Requires an AssistantLabs account. You sign in, choose which products ChatGPT can access, and can revoke access at any time.
• ChatGPT reaches one workspace: the one you choose when you sign in.
• Sending a message, publishing a post, pausing an ad, booking or cancelling is marked as an action, which ChatGPT can ask you to confirm.
• Some actions need a permission the owner ticks when connecting. Sending, changing contacts, booking, publishing, pausing ads and changing help desk tickets start unticked. Every tool still appears, and one whose permission is off says which permission it needs.
• Booking and cancelling can notify the customer.
• A new AI agent comes with a public chat page for trying it out. Customers reach it on WhatsApp, Instagram or your website only once you connect a channel, which is done in the AssistantLabs app.
• Adding a lead, changing a lead and logging an outcome only update the Leads board and send the lead nothing.
• On WhatsApp, a normal reply reaches the customer only within 24 hours of their last message. After that you need an approved WhatsApp template.
• Campaigns and launching ads are managed in the AssistantLabs app.
• ChatGPT can add and update the contacts your AI agent talks to. CRM companies are read only, and custom CRM records are not available here yet.
• Lists show customer names, who wrote, when, and who is waiting, without message text. A phone number or email appears only when you ask for it, or in your own business details.
• Phone numbers, emails, card numbers and ID numbers in common formats are automatically hidden inside messages. Don't use this plugin for medical records or other health data.

defaultPrompt: Set up my business on AssistantLabs
Build my AI agent from my website
Brief me: who is waiting for a reply and what is coming up?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

positive.description: List customers waiting for a reply. A read-only call. The tool returns each conversation's customer name, channel, time, who wrote last and `waiting`, which is true when the customer wrote last and nobody has answered. It returns no message text. The demo workspace holds conversations from the last few days.
positive.prompt: Who is waiting for a reply from us?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists recent conversations with the customer name, channel and time, and says which ones are waiting. No message text, phone number or email is returned, and nothing is sent.

positive.description: Check upcoming appointments. A read-only call. The demo workspace has appointments booked through the coming month. If none are booked, the tool says so. Those demo appointments carry no phone number or email.
positive.prompt: What appointments do we have coming up?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists upcoming appointments with time, service and customer name, or says none are booked. No phone number or email is returned.

positive.description: Find a topic in conversations and read one. search_conversations matches the exact words customers used, so this prompt says "the price", which is what the demo conversation says. The same conversation also contains the word "prices". get_conversation then reads the one the user picked.
positive.prompt: Which customers asked about the price this week? Read me the most recent one.
positive.expected_behavior: Names the conversations that mention the price, then shows what was said in the most recent one. Phone numbers and emails in common formats are automatically hidden inside the messages. Nothing is sent.

positive.description: Add a lead by hand. The prompt gives a phone number because add_lead needs a phone number or an email address. add_lead only writes the record: it sends nothing to the person, no automatic step runs, and the note goes on their record.
positive.prompt: Add Dana Levi, +972501234567, to the leads board. She called asking for a quote.
positive.expected_behavior: Dana Levi appears on the Leads board. The output shows her name and the note about the quote. Nothing is sent to her, and her phone number is not repeated in the output.

positive.description: Give the AI agent a new instruction. set_extra_instructions with add puts the note after the instructions already there, so nothing has to be read back first. This changes what the AI agent says to customers in future. It does not message anyone.
positive.prompt: Tell my customer-service agent that from now on, deliveries take 3 business days.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds the delivery rule to the agent's instructions and confirms it. The existing instructions are not returned, and no customer is messaged.

positive.description: Check where setup stands. A read-only call. The tool returns the same four setup steps the AssistantLabs app shows, each done or open, the products on this connection, the agent and its chat page, and each channel and tool picked with where it stands. The demo workspace has an agent and connected channels.
positive.prompt: Where does my AssistantLabs setup stand?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the workspace's setup steps as done or open, names the agent, and lists what is still open with the screen that finishes it. Nothing is changed or sent.

negative.description: Moving money is not supported: no tool can transfer funds, so the plugin must not trigger.
negative.prompt: Transfer 500 shekels from my bank account to my supplier.

negative.description: Data outside the signed-in account: tools only reach the user's own workspace, so the plugin returns no other business's data.
negative.prompt: Show me the customer list of another business that uses AssistantLabs.

negative.description: Unrelated request: nothing to do with running this business, so the plugin must not trigger.
negative.prompt: Book me a flight to London next week.

publication.release_notes:
What changed in 1.2.0:
- Setup in ChatGPT: the same four setup steps as the AssistantLabs app. A new owner can build their AI agent here from their website, a document, past conversations or a few questions (read_website, create_agent, then the existing agent tools), pick their channels and tools, and get one link to the app's connect window. Connecting a channel or a tool still happens in the AssistantLabs app.
- New tools: get_workspace_setup, save_setup_picks, read_website, create_agent, generate_test_customer_message, get_integration_meeting_offer, dismiss_integration_meeting_offer, ask_assistantlabs_support, get_assistantlabs_support_conversation. create_agent is marked as an action and open world, because the new agent comes with a public chat page.
- A start skill, set as the onboarding skill, runs setup one step at a time. It names no plans, prices or trials, and offers a setup call only when the owner asks for help or a step is stuck.
- A connection now also reaches the agents its owner creates after connecting, so an agent built in the app no longer needs a reconnect.
- Starter prompts: "Set up my business on AssistantLabs", "Build my AI agent from my website", and the daily brief.
